newsitem.title: UK: British Gas shareholders approve demerger.
newsitem.headline: British Gas shareholders approve demerger.

text.p: British Gas shareholders on Wednesday voted to approve the company's demerger, which will see the hiving off of its gas supply arm into a new company, Centrica Plc.
Shareholders also agreed to change the name of the British Gas rump, which will house its transportation business TransCo and its international operations, to BG Plc.

British Gas, which originated in the late 1940s and was privatised in 1986, said the demerger was an important step towards fighting increased competition in the UK market and resisting regulatory pressure to split the company.

"We believe that we should take the initiative in separating the competitive trading business from the monopoly transportation system, rather than wait until we are forced to do so," chairman Richard Giordano told shareholders at a special meeting.
The demerger was first announced a year ago and aims to protect the profitable transportation business from the burden of competition in the trading and domestic supply arm.
Competition was introduced in the UK market for big industrial users in 1991 and British Gas has consequently seen its share of that market dwindle to below 35 percent.
Competition was introduced last year to the household market through a pilot project in south west England, and is scheduled to be opened up nationwide by 1998.

As well as the gas supply business, Centrica will house British Gas' Morecombe Bay gas fields off northwest England. BG will comprise Transco, British Gas' exploration and production activities and its international gas business.
Shares in the two companies started trading on a grey market, when-issued basis, on Monday, and are due to trade unconditionally from next Monday, February 17. ($1=.6120 Pound)
